sections.heading: Array
sections.markdown: The new-XIR Array subset admits typed and homogeneous literals, contextual empty literals, ordinary logical copies, parameters/returns, index reads/writes and the27 structured member operations listed in spec §14.7. Its complete32-member inventory consists of30 instance methods, withCapacity and capacity. sort() currently accepts only zero-argument ascending Array<i64> calls; comparator arguments and other element types remain rejected. The five unadmitted instance methods are iterator, entriesIterator, ptr, mutPtr and toString. Array is a value struct; COW preserves independent copies. Borrowed slices and pointer/iterator protocols require their own admission and lifetime validation. Member admission does not replace full safety, resource or performance qualification.

sections.heading: Map
sections.markdown: Use {key: value} with expression keys and homogeneous key/value types or an explicit admitted context. Duplicate explicit keys reject; Map spreads overwrite in written order without erasing explicit-key provenance.

sections.heading: Set
sections.markdown: Construct a Set from an Array with Set([1, 2, 3]); empty Set() requires an element type or context.

sections.heading: Nominal struct / dynamic JSON object
sections.markdown: Fixed fields belong to nominal struct or class declarations, or unlabelled tuple values. Anonymous objects, shape types, width constraints and object patterns are removed. Dynamic JSON objects use JSON.Object, the alias for Map<string, JSON.Value>; JSON domain admission remains separate from inventory presence.

sections.heading: Index access
sections.markdown: For the new-XIR Array subset, get/index reads return independently owned elements and bounds are strict: 0 <= index < len. E0430 preserves the signed index and observed length. Index reads preserve the receiver selected before index evaluation; writes resolve the current root after argument/RHS evaluation. Set/push return unit, while index assignment returns the converted RHS. Len reads length without allocation or element traversal. See spec §17.26 for ownership and qualification limits.

sections.heading: Other collection-like types
bullets: `Array<u8>` is a typed byte buffer backed by contiguous memory
